hints.identity.height_read: how tall they read against people and furniture
hints.identity.speech: language + accent in a few words
hints.face.nose: the shape, and what must not drift
hints.face.facial_hair: default state; what it is never
hints.face.hair: colour, length, how it is worn, finish
hints.body.silhouette: proportion — usually the single most reliable on-model cue
hints.body.chest_and_shoulders: width across the shoulders, how the chest reads, where it tapers
hints.body.back: taper, lats, blades, spinal furrow — the body angle image shot from behind has nothing else to check itself against
hints.body.arms: length and thickness, how defined, where the muscle actually sits
hints.body.hands: palm and finger shape, nails, veins, hair; which wrist wears what
hints.body.neck: thickness AND length, the muscles that show, where facial hair stops
hints.body.midsection: how defined, honestly — "trim" and "shredded" are not the same
hints.body.lower_body: thighs, calves, hips; the shape, not just the size
hints.body.feet: size and shape — only ever read by a body angle that shows them
hints.body.body_hair: state it explicitly if it matters — generators default to smooth
hints.wardrobe.tops.detail: colour, cut, any embroidery or graphic
hints.wardrobe.lower_body: trousers, shorts or skirt — cut, length and colour
hints.wardrobe.footwear: the shoes they are usually in, and their colour
hints.wardrobe.accessories: the repeated ones — these carry recognition; say which wrist, how worn
hints.wardrobe.palette: the colours the character and their world live in
hints.voice.language: language spoken lines are written in
hints.voice.accent: the accent by name, and how strong it is
hints.voice.accent_cues: one sound or word the accent lands on
hints.consistency.must: one cue every render must show — the checklist, one line each
hints.consistency.never: what must be absent, or must never change
hints.consistency.drift_modes.fix: what to state in the prompt instead
hints.text_identity_block: ~50-70 words for engines that carry no reference images — only what a text-only engine cannot infer. `studio character textblock <name>` prints the raw material
hints.wardrobe.tops: ordered by how often the character wears it; the first is what a reference angle wears
hints.consistency.drift_modes: how models get this character wrong, each paired with the fix to write into the next prompt
hints.rendering.default_style: a preset name from studio-media-prompt's style presets
hints.rendering.optional_styles: other presets this character may opt into
